composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeEmail

normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeTelephone

normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeAddress

normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDuplicateTelephone

rejectDuplicateTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDuplicateTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDuplicateHousehold

rejectDuplicateHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDuplicateHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectCityAtCapacity

rejectCityAtCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectCityAtCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectOverDailyLimit

rejectOverDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectOverDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountOwnerNamesakes
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

content.text:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change mirrors the existing `RejectCityAtCapacity` trio (function + exception + handler + escalation YAML) exactly, which is the established pattern for this create pipeline:

- `RejectOverDailyLimit` is a single-purpose function class with one public `service` method, a `DAILY_LIMIT` constant, and the same `@Val Owner` + `OwnerRepository` signature and `findAll().stream().filter(...).count()` shape as its sibling `RejectCityAtCapacity`. Logic sits in the right unit.
- `DailyOwnerLimitExceededException` (checked, single-message constructor) and `DailyOwnerLimitExceededExceptionHandler` (using the shared `ProblemDetails.build` helper, `@Parameter` + `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>>`) match the surrounding escalation classes precisely. No catch-all handler was expanded; a dedicated exception/handler pair is the convention here.
- Pipeline wiring is correctly additive — a new `rejectOverDailyLimit` step slotted among the other reject-* steps, before `save`, with consistent `govern: [ transaction ]`, and the comment correctly notes it runs before the owner is persisted so the new owner isn't counted.
- The escalation YAML and naming (`RejectOverDailyLimit`, verb-plus-entity style) follow the documented conventions.

Nothing is duplicated beyond the deliberate per-concern mirroring the codebase already uses. A maintainer would find this natural.
